name: Mikie Sherrill
subject: 5 quick reasons
body:
[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250628-1?refcode=em-20250628-1&refcode2=235_1086043_2t8ZCn&akid=235%2E1086043%2E2t8ZCn ]Mikie Sherrill

Peter, it’s been a
few weeks since I won the Democratic nomination for governor of New
Jersey. But this race is already a rollercoaster — we’ve seen an
outpouring of grassroots support and also faced a barrage of right-wing
attacks.

With the key deadlines and the end of the quarter approaching, I need your
help to stop MAGA Republicans from flipping New Jersey red, and I’m humbly
asking you to [ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250628-1?refcode=em-20250628-1&refcode2=235_1086043_2t8ZCn&akid=235%2E1086043%2E2t8ZCn ]split $10 between my team and Wes Moore to
power our campaign to victory. But if you’re not sure (which I
understand!), here are five reasons I hope will convince you:

1) New Jersey is not a safe Democratic state anymore — far from it. The
last governor’s election here? It was decided by 3%. New Jersey’s margin
in the 2024 presidential election? 6%. The latest polling in this race
since we entered the general election? It shows me leading my GOP opponent
by only 3%.

2) Donald Trump is going to do everything he can to defeat me in this
race. He’s already endorsed my opponent, Jack Ciattarelli, and led a rally
for him — meaning MAGA money from all over the country is going to pour
into Ciattarelli’s campaign.

3) Unlike my opponent, I won’t ever hesitate to stand up to Trump when he
attacks New Jersey families. I’ve sworn an oath to the Constitution, and
I’ve spent my career honoring it to the best of my ability every single
day — before loyalty to any other politician or political party.
Ciattarelli has already made clear that his number-one priority is staying
in Trump’s good graces.

4) My top priority as governor will be making life more affordable for New
Jersey families. I’ve put forward detailed plans for lowering the cost of
everything from housing and energy to health care, child care, and
groceries — and I’m going to hit the ground running on Day 1 making them a
reality.

5) The stakes of this race are high not only for New Jersey, but for the
country. This is our chance to show the entire nation that the people
reject the Trump administration’s incompetence and authoritarianism. And
it’s our chance to get started on a better path forward — one where we
prioritize doing what’s best for working families over what’s best for
billionaires and corrupt political allies. There is no more important
bellwether ahead of 2026.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250628-1?refcode=em-20250628-1&refcode2=235_1086043_2t8ZCn&akid=235%2E1086043%2E2t8ZCn ]If any of these reasons speaks to you, I hope you will split a
$10 end-of-quarter donation between my team and Wes Moore to
help me defeat my Trump-endorsed opponent in this incredibly competitive
election to determine who leads our state for the next four years.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250628-1?amount=10&refcode=em-20250628-1&refcode2=235_1086043_2t8ZCn&akid=235%2E1086043%2E2t8ZCn ]Donate $10 ››

Thanks for reading, and have a great rest of your day.

-Mikie

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

This past week, I spoke with Lawrence O'Donnell on MSNBC about this final push by Trump and his lackeys to pass the Republican "Big Beautiful Bill for Billionaires."

**As early as next week, we could be voting to send this awful legislation, which would cut healthcare and food support for children to fund tax breaks for billionaires, to Trump's desk.** **Simply put: this is it. We need to do all we can to try and stop this NOW.** I will continue to fight back against this abomination with everything I have, but Republicans have made it clear what their priorities are in the majority: helping billionaire donors while screwing over working families and neighborhoods like those I represent in Philadelphia. **If we want to stop this kind of warped mentality, we need to take back Congress next year, plain and simple.** We need to elect Democrats who will prioritize real Americans, not the Elon Musks of the world. I'm working every day to help recruit and support Democrats to beat Republicans next year, but we need to be in this together if we want to succeed. **We're hitting the end of our fundraising quarter in a few days, and I'm hoping you can stand with me and help support the work we're doing? ** **Our average personal donation is less than $30, so every bit of support helps!** Sincerely, Congressman Brendan Boyle

Derek,

We are living in an unprecedented moment in modern American history. Under the Trump administration, we are witnessing oligarchs taking over our government, a rapid movement towards authoritarianism and a massive attack on programs that working people desperately need — such as Medicaid, Social Security, the Veterans Administration, housing and nutrition.

As we determine all the best ways to fight back, one thing is certain. Now is NOT the time for thinking small. Now is NOT the time to rely on the same old ideas, the same old politics, the same old establishment politicians.

name: A.G. Holder
subject: The birthplace of Juneteenth

body:
This Juneteenth, the march toward true, lived freedom continues.
|
---

Peter,
Juneteenth marks the day the news of freedom finally reached Black Americans in Galveston, Texas — two and a half full years _after_ President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation.
This Juneteenth, the 160th anniversary, holds a heavier weight for me. Across the country, we are witnessing attempts to suppress the ability to build a truly representative, multi-racial democracy — a direct threat to some of the very freedoms that this Freedom Day commemorates.
In Texas, where the celebration of Juneteenth was born, **partisan and racial gerrymandering lives and thrives**.
Texas was already being sued for violating the U.S. Constitution and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act by diluting the voting power of the state’s communities of color.
And just this month, the news broke that President Trump is actively pressuring Texas lawmakers to redraw its already-gerrymandered congressional map in an effort to gain an even more extreme partisan advantage.
On this poignant and powerful anniversary, let’s recommit to the notion that **our freedom is directly proportional to our power at the ballot box**. Let us remember that Juneteenth is not only a celebration, but a reminder that the march toward true, lived freedom is far from over.
Ours is a righteous fight, and I’m proud to be part of it alongside you.
In service,
Eric H. Holder, Jr.
82nd Attorney General of the United States

clean_body: This Juneteenth, the march toward true, lived freedom continues. | Peter, Juneteenth marks the day the news of freedom finally reached Black Americans in Galveston, Texas — two and a half full years after President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation. This Juneteenth, the 160th anniversary, holds a heavier weight for me. Across the country, we are witnessing attempts to suppress the ability to build a truly representative, multi-racial democracy — a direct threat to some of the very freedoms that this Freedom Day commemorates. In Texas, where the celebration of Juneteenth was born, partisan and racial gerrymandering lives and thrives. Texas was already being sued for violating the U.S. Constitution and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act by diluting the voting power of the state’s communities of color. And just this month, the news broke that President Trump is actively pressuring Texas lawmakers to redraw its already-gerrymandered congressional map in an effort to gain an even more extreme partisan advantage. On this poignant and powerful anniversary, let’s recommit to the notion that our freedom is directly proportional to our power at the ballot box. Let us remember that Juneteenth is not only a celebration, but a reminder that the march toward true, lived freedom is far from over. Ours is a righteous fight, and I’m proud to be part of it alongside you. In service, Eric H. Hey, this is Vivek Ramaswamy, and I'd like to share a personal story with you.
When I was in middle school, my father got laid off from his factory job at the General Electric plant in Evendale, Ohio. He was one of the hardest workers there, but like thousands of other good men and women, he was laid off without warning.
Most people would complain, whine, and stomp their feet, saying, "It's not fair!".
But not MY dad. He didn't cry about victimhood or racism.
Instead, he picked himself up, dusted himself off, got a new job, and enrolled in night school law classes for the next four years.
But because money was tight, he and my mother couldn't afford childcare. Every day after middle school, my dad would pick me up and we'd drive for 45 minutes to the University of Kentucky across the river.
I'd sit in the back of his law school classes every night.
Most kids my age would hate the idea of spending all day at school just to go to ANOTHER school at night. But not me.
I was FASCINATED, learning about the Constitution, the principles of law, and Supreme Court decisions.
So why do I even share this story with you in the first place?
Because that time in my life taught me a lesson I've never forgotten: Every hardship is an opportunity - if you're willing to work for it.
That mindset is the foundation of my campaign.
I don't believe in a culture of victimhood. I believe in the American Dream. I believe in merit over DEI. In hard work over handouts. In family, faith, and responsibility, not grievance and blame.
Right now, we have a real opportunity to reverse Radical Leftist policies. An opportunity to show how the nuclear family is the best form of governance. An opportunity to showcase how capitalism lifts people out of poverty. An opportunity to reinstate the American Dream.

clean_body: I love this photo of my dad and me at my Harvard graduation. He didn't just chase the American Dream - he passed it down. Hey, this is Vivek Ramaswamy, and I'd like to share a personal story with you. When I was in middle school, my father got laid off from his factory job at the General Electric plant in Evendale, Ohio. He was one of the hardest workers there, but like thousands of other good men and women, he was laid off without warning. Most people would complain, whine, and stomp their feet, saying, "It's not fair!". But not MY dad. He didn't cry about victimhood or racism. Instead, he picked himself up, dusted himself off, got a new job, and enrolled in night school law classes for the next four years. But because money was tight, he and my mother couldn't afford childcare. Every day after middle school, my dad would pick me up and we'd drive for 45 minutes to the University of Kentucky across the river. I'd sit in the back of his law school classes every night. Most kids my age would hate the idea of spending all day at school just to go to ANOTHER school at night. But not me. I was FASCINATED, learning about the Constitution, the principles of law, and Supreme Court decisions. So why do I even share this story with you in the first place? Because that time in my life taught me a lesson I've never forgotten: Every hardship is an opportunity - if you're willing to work for it. That mindset is the foundation of my campaign. I don't believe in a culture of victimhood. I believe in the American Dream. I believe in merit over DEI. In hard work over handouts. In family, faith, and responsibility, not grievance and blame. Right now, we have a real opportunity to reverse Radical Leftist policies. An opportunity to show how the nuclear family is the best form of governance. An opportunity to showcase how capitalism lifts people out of poverty. An opportunity to reinstate the American Dream. And I know that you're one of the dedicated American Patriots who believe in that vision. That's why I need you with me, Fellow American. Don't let our nation turn into one full of victims. body:
Derek, I know you’re busy so I’ll try and keep this quick.
I’ve been thinking: in my time in politics, there has never been anything as challenging, bizarre, and chaotic as the second Trump administration. Trump holding a $45 million military parade on his birthday... Trump ignoring court orders... Trump refusing to fire Pete Hegseth... Trump backing the largest cuts to Medicaid in history to fund tax breaks for the richest Americans.
But do you know what I’m realizing is even more bizarre? How many of my Republican colleagues in the Senate stay silent through it all. How they put Trump above the courts, the Constitution, even above their voters.
If my Republican colleagues can’t find their voice and speak out against this dangerous chaos, they prove that taking back the Senate for Democrats is the only way we can hold Trump accountable.
That’s why I’m asking if you’ll split a donation between my reelection campaign and Tim Kaine before our important end-of-quarter fundraising deadline at midnight on Monday. subject: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday: Phonebank to stop Medicaid cuts
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Working Families Party PAC (77 Sands St
body:
Your stories, your voices, and your calls are all having an impact. | | | Peter, **Republican Senators are planning to bring their budget reconciliation bill to a final vote in the next few days.** They are trying their best to ram through this legislation that would steal health care and food assistance away from millions and give handouts to the wealthy, all so Trump can sign it into law before July 4th. **But it’s not proving as easy as they hoped.** Over the last few days, Senate Republicans have faced several setbacks to their proposed cuts:
* The Senate parliamentarian has ruled that some of the cuts cannot be passed through reconciliation,1
* Several GOP Senators have gone on record with concerns about the Medicaid cuts as they stand,2
* **And voters are saying they disapprove of the Republican budget by _massive margins_ in multiple recent polls.**3

**Your stories, your voices, and your work to keep the pressure on Congress are all having an impact.** But with Republicans trying to jam this bill through as fast as possible, there are only a few days left to stop them from passing these cuts that would devastate families. **** [**Working Families Power, MoveOn, Indivisible, and Community Change Action are holding more phonebanks next Monday 6/30, Tuesday 7/1, and Wednesday 7/2 to have one-on-one conversations with Medicaid recipients and urge them to contact their own members of Congress directly. Sign up here and help make calls on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday!**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJuplBE8nUpvXhdUbWUJpQhWISJ-zuNdSO_iroX67V-d3OTxEg3yPGmN1n8EbmNIepxgsb8UWzjZDTj6fGMROs7OU1Og-3Y90Wr6ShgMMiOBkGB_qNgY_DYvPfPhny13zYGvQ4E86rO9-bTtp-6cbT6TYBX8lfsh4ZVv0OoNiS15yj-6wS8Ubvs29h_LPpHVoGACeDTt-ML2VfNk3gqSbiu9IdtDcXRI9f6kmj5idQOxVy4SR0sPfMH3iAcvNlSQ4GnTDOxuFrN5Ia2CJoHotXG/4hq/orVEJ4WXTye3APsFRt4eng/h0/h001.GQVAjSvgj5MTwZQ9ia_NPPZU0waDGP5zzMT_Ud-VXUA) **[Sign up to phonebank »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJuplBE8nUpvXhdUbWUJpQhWISJ-zuNdSO_iroX67V-d3OTxEg3yPGmN1n8EbmNIeoSu9KSWlrbrrPEh5X1yks1MHXea9MUBp5jXptWQvts74vuJ8j1Fkr5TEfACaasZHXBcCAJT7NEAM6dq1ttY7FtHq1UirPagp5wZlkNGeL-D3UDJdh-JRJqY6HYIs9G0mtKyULGpzQ6Ll0IrvkEIWvycGesDCYPAcnrMHTnf2lOhVdg0s0-Yb2YhrWCstjsyBlMypggwbTV7yLAdJutHBjO/4hq/orVEJ4WXTye3APsFRt4eng/h1/h001.krUKAT1kDjGElgD5A_Wy573UPAa09GKI8roPWF6G5Gw)** Republicans in Congress want to make life even harder for working families in order to give their campaign donors huge tax breaks. **But the more they hear from their own constituents about what these cuts would mean to them, the more worried they are getting.** You can help keep it up. clean_body: Your stories, your voices, and your calls are all having an impact. | | | Peter, Republican Senators are planning to bring their budget reconciliation bill to a final vote in the next few days. They are trying their best to ram through this legislation that would steal health care and food assistance away from millions and give handouts to the wealthy, all so Trump can sign it into law before July 4th. But it’s not proving as easy as they hoped. Over the last few days, Senate Republicans have faced several setbacks to their proposed cuts: The Senate parliamentarian has ruled that some of the cuts cannot be passed through reconciliation,1 Several GOP Senators have gone on record with concerns about the Medicaid cuts as they stand,2 And voters are saying they disapprove of the Republican budget by massive margins in multiple recent polls.3 Your stories, your voices, and your work to keep the pressure on Congress are all having an impact. But with Republicans trying to jam this bill through as fast as possible, there are only a few days left to stop them from passing these cuts that would devastate families. Republicans in Congress want to make life even harder for working families in order to give their campaign donors huge tax breaks. But the more they hear from their own constituents about what these cuts would mean to them, the more worried they are getting. You can help keep it up. Thank you for being with us in this fight. clean_body: It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us. | Fellow Conservative, I’m Adam Schwarze—former Navy SEAL Officer, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan. I’ve deployed nine times to 70 countries to serve this great country. I never expected to run for the U.S. Senate. But when I returned home and saw what was happening to Minnesota—when I saw the radical left rising—I knew I had to step up. And now I need your help. The same Democratic Socialist movement that just This week, New York Democrats nominated a man so extreme that he promised to arrest the Israeli Prime Minister and replace city police with social workers. If that sounds insane, it is. But don’t think it’s limited to the coasts.** My opponent—the lieutenant governor of Minnesota—isn’t far behind. She openly aligned with violent unrest in 2020, pushed to dismantle our police, and filed lawsuits against law enforcement as our communities burned. While Governor Walz tried to save face, she doubled down on chaos. This kind of radicalism isn’t an outlier anymore. It’s the new blueprint of the left. And if we don’t draw the line in Minnesota, it will keep spreading. The Minnesota I grew up in—where you respected your neighbors, honored your country, and stood for law and order—feels like it’s slipping away. I didn’t wait to serve my country after 9/11. I enlisted on my 18th birthday and spent over 20 years protecting American freedom abroad. Now I’m fighting to protect it at home. I don’t come from money or a political legacy. I come from grit, faith, and a calling to serve. That’s what drives me now. It may be too late for New York, but there is still hope for the rest of us. This election isn’t just about one Senate seat. It’s about stopping a national wave of socialist extremism that threatens to bankrupt small businesses, rewrite our values, and destroy what millions of Americans fought and died to defend. New York may have fallen to it. But Minnesota doesn’t have to. If you’ve ever felt like your voice doesn’t matter anymore, it does. The radical left is organized, loud, and well-funded. But they don’t speak for most of us. We need a new kind of leadership—rooted in service, not self-interest. If you’re not ready to donate today, that’s okay. While Trump and the media battle over whether Iran's nuclear sites were "ANNIHILATED," the focus on BDA (Battle Damage Assessment) is missing the forest for the trees. First off, every American should be thrilled that, while on the precipice, we were able to avoid falling into yet another power vacuum used to justify yet another regime-change forever war in the Middle East.
Did Iran's uranium enrichment centrifuges get obliterated into itty bitty smithereens? Probably. Is Iran's nuclear program delayed by months or even years? Yes. Did we avoid putting boots on the ground? Yes. Did Iran and Israel cease bombing each other? YES. These three affirmatives are what matter most at this time.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..8WzDdHoIHS_LuQtnVwVsmSzkkcH_13yyLqr0Rnla7Zg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=167019503)
I am 35, old enough to remember when the Democrats were supposed to be the party of anti-war. But these days, if Trump says peace, they say war. If Trump says bomb, they say don't. On issues as monumental as nuclear bombs, our political conversation is fixated on stirring up the bathwater while the baby was thrown out during the spring invasion of Baghdad in 2003.
When it comes to a place with as much history as the Middle East, every struggle is in increments and every battle is in inches. Cyrus the Great unified Persia over 2,500 years ago when his armies defeated Nabonidus and the Neo-Babylonian Empire. The Assyrians conquered the Israelites; the Israelites conquered the Canaanites. The Ottomans fought the Persians for three hundred years. The Russians fought the Persians for centuries. MI-6 and the CIA backed a coup d'etat that overthrew the populist socialist Prime Minister Mohammad Mossaddegh and reinstated the pro-Western monarchy of the Shah.

Be loud. Be proud. Be legendary.

**(Piece continues below)**
A quarter of a century later, the pendulum swung the other way, and now the Russians are on the Iranian (modern Persian) side and the Brits and the Americans are backing the Israelis, who have possessed nukes since the eve of the '67 Six Day War. The Arabs refer to this devastating loss as Al-Naksa, which means the Setback. Three different Arab nations were decimated in less than a week, and yet it is referred to as a mere "setback". That's because over there, battles are waged across generations. Meanwhile, we Americans measure the arc of history in election cycles and markets that shift as quickly as the dunes roll all the way to the strait of Hormuz.
I could go on for a thousand more pages, but I think you get the point: the tribal and sectarian divisions of the blood-stained land run deeper than the oil below. Our American minds are too young to understand the depths of these conflicts and too ambitious to care.
What it comes down to is dollar signs. Big surprise, Iran's promise to shutter the straight of Hormuz were idle threats because they sell 90 percent of their oil exports to China; China didn't want them to shut it and so they did not. I'm just happy as long as those dollar signs don't equate to putting boots on the ground and nation building on the backs and through the blood of our youngest and strongest men.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..8WzDdHoIHS_LuQtnVwVsmSzkkcH_13yyLqr0Rnla7Zg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=167019503)
I was 45 miles from Manhattan on 9/11/2001 and through my formative years I watched our bloodthirsty and greedy government initiate two disastrous wars. I spent six months living in the Middle East while studying Arabic for two hours per day, five days per week for three years. I had labored to learn the language with hopes of somehow undoing or fixing these horrible mistakes. But when I got back stateside from my study abroad, I said the same thing as Trump, "We basically have two countries that have been fighting so long and so hard that they don't know what the fuck they're doing."
Pardon the less-than Presidential language, but in this case the words are fitting and Trump is right.
If we examine what happened after the NATO-imposed "no fly zone" in Libya, for example, the unintended consequences of regime change are clear. At the time, Libya had one of the highest per-capita incomes in Africa. Then Ghaddafi was executed via a bayonet in his ass, and the country has been embroiled in civil war ever since.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..8WzDdHoIHS_LuQtnVwVsmSzkkcH_13yyLqr0Rnla7Zg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=167019503)
When it comes to the question of American use of force in the Middle East, we cannot allow the perfect to be the enemy of the good. Almost none of the idiots you see squawking about BDA on cable news have any clue what's really going on over there, nor do they care. Half of them are blinded by Trump derangement syndrome, and the other half are still clinging to their provably catastrophic Neo Conservative desires.
Let's pack up and get back to addressing our own problems. Let's be thankful that, for the moment, we are no longer teetering on toppling another government in the near east, and we are (at least in the case of Iran) no longer on the brink of nuclear war. In the meantime, Iran has a lot of work to do if they want to get a nuclear weapon, and Israel has hangered its plane and sheathed its sword. Unlike our domestic politics, when it comes to the Middle East, I will take a kick of the can down the road over a thermonuclear war.

But these days, if Trump says peace, they say war... | | | Jun 28| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- While Trump and the media battle over whether Iran's nuclear sites were "ANNIHILATED," the focus on BDA (Battle Damage Assessment) is missing the forest for the trees. First off, every American should be thrilled that, while on the precipice, we were able to avoid falling into yet another power vacuum used to justify yet another regime-change forever war in the Middle East. Did Iran's uranium enrichment centrifuges get obliterated into itty bitty smithereens? Probably. Is Iran's nuclear program delayed by months or even years? Yes. Did we avoid putting boots on the ground? Yes. Did Iran and Israel cease bombing each other? YES. These three affirmatives are what matter most at this time. I am 35, old enough to remember when the Democrats were supposed to be the party of anti-war. But these days, if Trump says peace, they say war. If Trump says bomb, they say don't. On issues as monumental as nuclear bombs, our political conversation is fixated on stirring up the bathwater while the baby was thrown out during the spring invasion of Baghdad in 2003. When it comes to a place with as much history as the Middle East, every struggle is in increments and every battle is in inches. Cyrus the Great unified Persia over 2,500 years ago when his armies defeated Nabonidus and the Neo-Babylonian Empire. The Assyrians conquered the Israelites; the Israelites conquered the Canaanites. The Ottomans fought the Persians for three hundred years. The Russians fought the Persians for centuries. MI-6 and the CIA backed a coup d'etat that overthrew the populist socialist Prime Minister Mohammad Mossaddegh and reinstated the pro-Western monarchy of the Shah. A message from our sponsor (piece continues below) Hey Patriot, This 4th of July, don't just celebrate freedom -- | | ---|---|--- The Official Trump Sneakers are making waves across the country... 🔥 Worn by patriots 🔥 Designed to turn heads 🔥 Selling out fast These limited-edition kicks aren't just sneakers -- they're a A stand for what you believe in. And the perfect gift for any America-loving conservative. Crafted with pride. Built to last. | | ---|---|--- Be loud. Be proud. Be legendary. (Piece continues below) A quarter of a century later, the pendulum swung the other way, and now the Russians are on the Iranian (modern Persian) side and the Brits and the Americans are backing the Israelis, who have possessed nukes since the eve of the '67 Six Day War. The Arabs refer to this devastating loss as Al-Naksa, which means the Setback. Three different Arab nations were decimated in less than a week, and yet it is referred to as a mere "setback". That's because over there, battles are waged across generations. Meanwhile, we Americans measure the arc of history in election cycles and markets that shift as quickly as the dunes roll all the way to the strait of Hormuz. I could go on for a thousand more pages, but I think you get the point: the tribal and sectarian divisions of the blood-stained land run deeper than the oil below. Our American minds are too young to understand the depths of these conflicts and too ambitious to care. What it comes down to is dollar signs. Big surprise, Iran's promise to shutter the straight of Hormuz were idle threats because they sell 90 percent of their oil exports to China; China didn't want them to shut it and so they did not. I'm just happy as long as those dollar signs don't equate to putting boots on the ground and nation building on the backs and through the blood of our youngest and strongest men. I was 45 miles from Manhattan on 9/11/2001 and through my formative years I watched our bloodthirsty and greedy government initiate two disastrous wars. I spent six months living in the Middle East while studying Arabic for two hours per day, five days per week for three years. I had labored to learn the language with hopes of somehow undoing or fixing these horrible mistakes. But when I got back stateside from my study abroad, I said the same thing as Trump, "We basically have two countries that have been fighting so long and so hard that they don't know what the fuck they're doing." Pardon the less-than Presidential language, but in this case the words are fitting and Trump is right. If we examine what happened after the NATO-imposed "no fly zone" in Libya, for example, the unintended consequences of regime change are clear. At the time, Libya had one of the highest per-capita incomes in Africa. Then Ghaddafi was executed via a bayonet in his ass, and the country has been embroiled in civil war ever since. When it comes to the question of American use of force in the Middle East, we cannot allow the perfect to be the enemy of the good. Almost none of the idiots you see squawking about BDA on cable news have any clue what's really going on over there, nor do they care. Half of them are blinded by Trump derangement syndrome, and the other half are still clinging to their provably catastrophic Neo Conservative desires. Let's pack up and get back to addressing our own problems. Let's be thankful that, for the moment, we are no longer teetering on toppling another government in the near east, and we are (at least in the case of Iran) no longer on the brink of nuclear war. In the meantime, Iran has a lot of work to do if they want to get a nuclear weapon, and Israel has hangered its plane and sheathed its sword. Unlike our domestic politics, when it comes to the Middle East, I will take a kick of the can down the road over a thermonuclear war. * PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. Dear Derek,
When I ran for Congress in 2018, I had never been a political candidate before, so I didn’t do politics the way things had always been done.
Political consultants asked me what I wanted to campaign on. When I said that my top issue was housing (after all, I had been a foreclosure fighter during the financial crisis), they said that that wasn’t really an issue that politicians focus on. I did it anyway.
After hearing me talk about being a minivan-driving single mom, another consultant commented that it would be so great if I actually had the van, so we could use it as a prop in a photoshoot. (Dude, it’s not a prop; it’s actually what I used to drive my three kids to school!)
When it came to financing my campaign, I committed from Day One to reject donations from corporate PACs, and despite doubts from some operatives, I’ve stuck to my promise.
All of this—doing politics differently and relentlessly focusing on what families need—is possible because of emails like this one and supporters like you.
When I sat down in those hearing rooms to ask tough questions of the witnesses before Congress, I knew I had the power of a grassroots movement behind me.
Ahead of our June fundraising deadline, when we’ll have to publicly report how much we’ve raised, I need your help again. **[Can you chip in $5 to show everyone that we can campaign differently than the way things have always been done—and win?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250628_1_ak?refcode=em20250628-39841&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39841_3422442_v-AZLP&akid=39841%2E3422442%2Ev-AZLP)**

—Katie

Peter – with just over 48 hours until my biggest fundraising deadline in months, and with the Senate voting on Trump's _Big, Ugly Bill_ at any moment,**[I'm asking you to chip in $5 today toward my $50,000 end-of-quarter goal.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110429755/554319530/-1711732667?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk524-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMGJmZTBiYS0zNDU0LWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yMrpA4wHkGdHWRMP2XX0OV1Ucj51KKJy38P_tciIDVA=)**
Because if we're going to keep up the fight to stop them from choking off health care coverage for millions of people, I need your help.
If we're going to keep up the fight to stop them from shutting down rural hospitals and clinics and pushing older Americans out of nursing homes, I need your help.
If we're going to keep up the fight to stop them from ripping lifesaving treatments, vital medications, and routine care from millions of people, I need your help.
If we're going to keep up the fight to stop them from forcing millions of kids, veterans, low-income workers, disabled folks, and our elders to go hungry, I need your help.
And if we're going to keep up the fight to stop them from letting Trump's tariffs send inflation sky-high, making you pay thousands of dollars more for the basics each year, I need your help.
Now you might be wondering: _How could my $5 possibly help Sen. Murray keep up the fight to stop Republicans' from passing this disastrous budget_ _ to fund Trump's agenda __– and kicking off the single largest transfer of wealth from the poor to the rich in U.S. history?_
(If you already know, then please, [**click here to chip in $5 or anything you can spare**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110429757/554319531/-1711732667?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk524-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMGJmZTBiYS0zNDU0LWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yMrpA4wHkGdHWRMP2XX0OV1Ucj51KKJy38P_tciIDVA=) –**** otherwise, give me just 30 more seconds of your time to explain.)
See, after 12 a.m., July 1, we are** required by law **to report our fundraising numbers from the last quarter to the FEC. Then, they'll be published online for everyone, including Trump, the GOP, and megadonors like Elon Musk, to see.
And believe me – they _will_ be looking.** **
So, will our numbers show there's a groundswell of support for Democrats to**stop** the GOP from shoveling money into the pockets of corporations and the richest 20% of Americans by robbing the poorest 80% _and_ adding trillions to the national debt?
Will they indicate that voters are **fed up** with the job they're doing in the other Washington – and that come next November, they may be out of a job entirely?
Or, will it show the GOP that we're not fired up enough to put up a fight against their agenda that throws health care, food stamps, veterans benefits, and so much more down the drain to fund Trump's _ Big, Ugly Bill_?

The history of the Roman Republic is a captivating tale of achievement, political and military genius, and the perils of success. One that still impacts our world today.

To help tell this important story to Americans nationwide, we released our free online course, **" The Rise and Fall of the Roman Republic."**

**You can now receive your own DVD box set of "The Rise and Fall of the Roman Republic" when you make a tax-deductible gift of $100 or more in support of our educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty.**

Friend, I’ve pushed back against political violence for years, introducing legislation to stop violence against women in politics. Two weeks ago, when a man in Minnesota shot and killed a state lawmaker and her spouse and tried to kill more lawmakers, it was revealed that he had a hit list with more elected officials as potential targets. And my name was on it. My family and I are safe, and I’m not letting this stop me from connecting with constituents or speaking truth to power. That day I went to multiple No Kings rallies in my district and encouraged people to stay in the streets resisting Trump. But at this time of increased political violence, my team and I need to take more precautions. That includes hiring a private security detail, including a driver when I am traveling around the district and meeting with constituents. We’ve also had to increase security protocols at our campaign headquarters to protect our staff and volunteers. **None of this security is handled by the federal government.** All of this must be paid for through our campaign. We need to budget roughly $1,000 a day when we have added security―which adds up since I’m out and about in my district every week, multiple days a week. We hadn’t planned on these expenses, but in order for me to continue speaking truth to power, they’re necessary. **We should all be able to express our political views without fear of violence. Two weeks ago, when a man in Minnesota shot and killed a state lawmaker and her spouse and tried to kill more lawmakers, it was revealed that he had a hit list with more elected officials as potential targets. And my name was on it. My family and I are safe, and I’m not letting this stop me from connecting with constituents or speaking truth to power. That day I went to multiple No Kings rallies in my district and encouraged people to stay in the streets resisting Trump. But at this time of increased political violence, my team and I need to take more precautions. That includes hiring a private security detail, including a driver when I am traveling around the district and meeting with constituents. We’ve also had to increase security protocols at our campaign headquarters to protect our staff and volunteers. None of this security is handled by the federal government. All of this must be paid for through our campaign. We need to budget roughly $1,000 a day when we have added security―which adds up since I’m out and about in my district every week, multiple days a week. We hadn’t planned on these expenses, but in order for me to continue speaking truth to power, they’re necessary. We should all be able to express our political views without fear of violence. body:
I want you to know where I stand:
| | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110435060/554331507/-922610151?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5557-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3Mzc1ZDA1Ni0zYTU0LWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hNsOlq2bhRy3T_0W3idhqrHVi-iSZC6zRKK-e3ziAQ0=)
Team — I’ve always believed that if any political candidate is going to ask you for your hard-earned money, they have an obligation to share with you exactly where they stand on key issues.
So if you have a moment, I’d like to share with you where I stand on three key issues in this race and how my position compares with my opponent’s. And if after reading this, your views align with mine, I hope you will [**split $5, or whatever amount works for you, between my campaign and Jacky Rosen's to help me end the quarter on a strong note and win what could be a nail-biter of an election.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110435062/554331509/-922610151?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5557-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3Mzc1ZDA1Ni0zYTU0LWYwMTEtOGY3Yy02MDQ1YmRmZThlOWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hNsOlq2bhRy3T_0W3idhqrHVi-iSZC6zRKK-e3ziAQ0=)
**Abortion rights**
**Where I stand:** The decision of if and when to start a family is one that every woman deserves to make for herself — period. As governor, I will work to permanently protect reproductive freedom in our state by enshrining the right to an abortion in New Jersey's state constitution, as well as stockpile mifepristone and strengthen protections for providers.

**Where my opponent stands:** He supports an abortion ban and wants to defund Planned Parenthood in New Jersey.
**Affordability**
**Where I stand:** My top priority is making every aspect of daily life more affordable for New Jerseyans — and I’ve put forward detailed plans on how to lower the cost of housing, health care, child care, energy, groceries, and the taxes that working families pay.

**Where my opponent stands:** Proudly alongside Trump as national Republicans try to cut Medicaid, endanger Medicare, take away food assistance, and give billionaires a massive tax break. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Jeff Bezos’ wedding
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Republicans would cut health care for more than 16 million people as Bezos celebrates his wedding on his $500 million superyacht.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2585%2E4032634%2ExsMaBv)
---
Right now, Jeff Bezos is renting out the city of Venice for his estimated $50 million wedding. At the same time, Republicans in Congress are debating a spending plan that would give billionaires like Bezos a massive tax break. **Here’s an uncontroversial opinion: If Jeff Bezos can rent out the city of Venice for his wedding, then he can pay more in taxes.** Despite the fact that billionaires are doing better than ever, Senate Republicans are essentially crying, _“Who will think of the poor billionaires?”_ with this budget. We could instead be discussing a budget bill that helps couples who are saving penny after penny to afford a nice wedding. A budget bill that helps families who are trying to buy their first home, or simply just want to be able to afford quality child care as they grow their family. A budget bill that helps public school teachers who pay a higher tax rate than Jeff Bezos. But, nope. Republicans in Congress aren’t interested in supporting working families. Their spending plan cuts health care and food benefits so the government can afford to give billionaires even more tax breaks. [**If you believe our government needs to pass policies that support working people — not subsidize multi-million-dollar weddings for Jeff Bezos — then please chip in $28 or anything you can right now to support our campaign. This fight isn’t over, and I’m doing everything I can in the Senate to get our government to actually work for working people.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3047?amount=28&t=8&akid=2585%2E4032634%2ExsMaBv)

---

---
Donald Trump ran a campaign on lowering costs for everyday working people. And yet he’s forcing through a bill that will jack up expenses on groceries and health care — all to fund massive giveaways to his billionaire backers. If passed, this bill would result in the largest transfer of wealth from the poor to the rich in our history. That’s on top of an economy that has already been working better and better for billionaires and the ultra-rich, and worse and worse for everyone else. The timing of Bezos’ wedding and this spending plan being debated on the same weekend is just cruel irony. Republicans would let more kids go hungry while Bezos rents out a fragile, historic city as his own private playground. Republicans would cut health care for more than 16 million people as Bezos celebrates his wedding on his $500 million superyacht. Republicans would make our energy costs go up and worsen the climate crisis by cutting clean energy investments — all while the richest people in the world fly their private jets into this event. **In the short-term, I’m doing everything I can to stop this bill from passing. But there’s still more we’ve got to do, and it’s called a wealth tax.** [**We need people in our government who fight for working people. That’s what I’m here to do every single day. If you’re able to, please chip in $28 or anything you can to support our campaign fighting to tax billionaires like Bezos more so that our economy and our country work for everyone.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3047?amount=28&t=14&akid=2585%2E4032634%2ExsMaBv) Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

body:
Being double-jointed came in handy

| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110438692/554342174/1328794144?refcode=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYxYjNhNTdiLTQwNTQtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZvG1-bGbQCX-XgaBhp50hLjdQ1LR7CLAM7BP1tGpFrI=&emci=b182c5d2-7a53-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ceid=4823105)
---
I'm sure you've seen the infamous mugshot of me from 1970. What you probably don't know is the story behind how I managed to raise my fist while in handcuffs. **[Before we dive into anything, I want to ask: Would you be able to chip in a few dollars before our biggest deadline of the year so far on June 30th? Every bit of support helps us elect real climate champions at a time when the stakes for our climate and our democracy have never been higher.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110438694/554342176/2105508926?refcode=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYxYjNhNTdiLTQwNTQtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZvG1-bGbQCX-XgaBhp50hLjdQ1LR7CLAM7BP1tGpFrI=)** [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110438696/554342178/2105508926?refcode=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYxYjNhNTdiLTQwNTQtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZvG1-bGbQCX-XgaBhp50hLjdQ1LR7CLAM7BP1tGpFrI=) _My infamous mugshot, taken in November 1970 in Cleveland, OH_ To make a long story short, I was arrested on fabricated drug smuggling charges. What they claimed were drugs were, in fact, vitamins. I kid you not. It turns out that the orders for my arrest came straight from the Nixon White House — it was a frame-up. After spending the night in jail in Cleveland, they took me to the courthouse the next morning. I was handcuffed, photographers were waiting, and I knew this was my moment to send a message. **Here's where being double-jointed came in handy: I made my hands really small, slipped right out of one handcuff before the policewoman knew what was happening, and threw up that “power to the people” fist you see in the photo.** That image became an enduring symbol of resistance that's still on t-shirts and protest signs today. And here's the thing — there was more to that gesture than just sticking it to the man. **I raised it because I believed then, like I believe now, that when powerful people try to silence you, you find a way to make your voice heard anyway.** That's exactly what JanePAC is all about. When Big Oil tries to buy our democracy, when Trump and his allies try to strip our freedoms to speak out for what we believe in, we find a way to fight back. The same spirit that got me out of those handcuffs in 1970 is what's driving our movement today. We're not backing down from this fight for our planet. **[Today, I'm asking you to carry forward that same spirit of resistance. With just two days left until our end-of-quarter deadline, every contribution helps us elect leaders who refuse to be silenced by Big Oil. Can I count on your support right now?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110438698/554342180/2105508926?refcode=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYxYjNhNTdiLTQwNTQtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZvG1-bGbQCX-XgaBhp50hLjdQ1LR7CLAM7BP1tGpFrI=)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | [**DONATE $5**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110438700/554342182/2105508926?express_lane=true&amount=5&refcode=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYxYjNhNTdiLTQwNTQtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZvG1-bGbQCX-XgaBhp50hLjdQ1LR7CLAM7BP1tGpFrI=) | [**DONATE $25**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/110438702/554342184/2105508926?express_lane=true&amount=25&refcode=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&ms=ea.f1b3a57b-4054-f011-8f7c-6045bdfe8e9c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImYxYjNhNTdiLTQwNTQtZjAxMS04ZjdjLTYwNDViZGZlOGU5YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZvG1-bGbQCX-XgaBhp50hLjdQ1LR7CLAM7BP1tGpFrI=)

clean_body: Being double-jointed came in handy | I'm sure you've seen the infamous mugshot of me from 1970. What you probably don't know is the story behind how I managed to raise my fist while in handcuffs. = = My infamous mugshot, taken in November 1970 in Cleveland, OH To make a long story short, I was arrested on fabricated drug smuggling charges. What they claimed were drugs were, in fact, vitamins. I kid you not. It turns out that the orders for my arrest came straight from the Nixon White House — it was a frame-up. After spending the night in jail in Cleveland, they took me to the courthouse the next morning. I was handcuffed, photographers were waiting, and I knew this was my moment to send a message. Here's where being double-jointed came in handy: I made my hands really small, slipped right out of one handcuff before the policewoman knew what was happening, and threw up that “power to the people” fist you see in the photo. That image became an enduring symbol of resistance that's still on t-shirts and protest signs today. And here's the thing — there was more to that gesture than just sticking it to the man. I raised it because I believed then, like I believe now, that when powerful people try to silence you, you find a way to make your voice heard anyway. That's exactly what JanePAC is all about. When Big Oil tries to buy our democracy, when Trump and his allies try to strip our freedoms to speak out for what we believe in, we find a way to fight back. The same spirit that got me out of those handcuffs in 1970 is what's driving our movement today. We're not backing down from this fight for our planet. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = ✊ Onward. – Jane Fonda = | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. body:
Jason Crow For Congress [https://nvlupin.blob.core.windows.net/images/van/NGP/NGP21/1/88523/images/logoJC%20(1).png]
Team,

This isn’t the email we hoped to send. But we want to be honest with you: We had to raise our end-of-quarter goal, and now we’re at risk of falling short.

We didn’t make this decision lightly. But the truth is, there’s just too much at stake.

Republicans are dead-set on ripping away health care, food assistance, and other essential services that hard-working Americans rely on — all to give a massive tax break to the wealthiest few.

Senate Republicans rolled out their own version of Trump’s so-called “Big, Beautiful Bill” – proposing even _bigger_ cuts to health care.
And on the tax front, guess what they proposed?
Tax cuts for billionaires.
That’s right: The GOP is trying to pass a budget bill that would rob up to 16 million Americans of their health care and raise costs on virtually every American – all to help billionaires get richer.
Why are they doing this? Well, in short: Because they think they can. Their bet is that they can deliver a windfall to the special interests who fund their campaigns – all without facing any political consequences.

If you’d like to unsubscribe, | | It's Caroline, Dr. Ruiz’s finance director. I need to be honest with you about where things stand — and right now, it’s not good. We’re hitting the summer slump. Every summer, our fundraising slows down, and this year, the summer slump is compounded by Californians’ fear and uncertainty about where Donald Trump is going to wreak havoc next. And with our FEC end-of-quarter fundraising deadline just over 48 hours away, this couldn’t be happening at a worse time. If we fall short now, Republicans will pull even further ahead — and once that happens, it’s almost impossible to catch up. I know times are tough and money is tight. But supporting candidates like Dr. Ruiz is exactly what we need to flip the House blue and get back to making real progress for California’s working people and families. Let’s be clear: if we don’t act now, Republicans will keep pushing their agenda — threatening our communities, undermining our democracy, and holding California and our country back. This isn’t just about one race. It’s about standing up for the values we believe in and fighting back against those who want to silence us and stall progress. body:
# [](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/203?t=1&akid=456%2E181023%2EYX9bh2)
Listen.
That’s what I’m doing. I’m on the road across Michigan, visiting small towns and large, east to west and north to south (yes, all the way up to our Upper Peninsula) to do what we all need to do more of: Listening.
What I hear every place I go is one refrain: people are struggling in this economy. Struggling to afford a home or pay for groceries, worried about living paycheck to paycheck, fearing what potential cuts to Medicaid could do to their life when they are already stretched so thin.
It is sobering. And it is infuriating.
But I am also left feeling a sense of optimism and hope. Hope for what we can do together and optimism for the simple fact that I’ve learned time and again defending democracy:
**The power of the people will always be greater than the people in power.**
From educators to small business owners to the nurses and healthcare providers, to the farmers and the families and the students and our seniors. People like you, and your friends and neighbors.
It reminds me why I’m in this, and who I’m in this for: I’m running for governor because I see our struggles and I want to do something about it.
**We can make Michigan the best place to be a kid, raise a kid, and call home. From taking our public education to the top 10, to expanding affordable housing, all the way to bringing high speed light rail to Michigan – I want to make sure everyone can thrive.**
[**Your support powers this work, and before our upcoming deadline, I hope you can pitch in a few dollars to help us keep this show on the road!**](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/854?c0=jmb-em-q22025.35DAUP&refcode=AU_JMB_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC_20250628_PM1_V1_S1&t=2&akid=456%2E181023%2EYX9bh2)

Dear Friend, Most of our state freedom caucuses are technically out of session heading into the summer. But that doesn't mean they stop working to defend your liberties. We have a lot to report today.
---
|
---
**WYOMING** The Wyoming Department of Health's website is recommending that "pregnant people" still get the COVID vaccine. Once the **Wyoming Freedom Caucus** was made aware of that, they publicly called out the Department of Health for this inexcusable wokeness and dogmatic support for the experimental shot. After feeling the heat, the Department updated their website to say "pregnant women". But the WYFC isn't going to take a victory lap. They will continue to hammer the Gordon Administration until they stop recommending the vaccine.
---
---
|
---
**ARIZONA** The **Arizona Freedom Caucus** just concluded an honorable fight against the Phoenix Swamp on the state budget this week. Earlier this month, they forced the State House to pass a conservative budget with meaningful, conservative reforms in it. Despite having a Republican majority, the State Senate ignored that budget, and insisted on proceeding with the bill its leadership had negotiated in a backroom deal with Democrat Governor Katie Hobbs.Since the two chambers were at a stalemate, GOP leadership in both the House and Senate decided to advance the bloated budget they had been crafting behind closed doors. This boondoggle budget grows spending by 8.6% and has no meaningful reforms in it. Their backroom deal was rammed through the House and Senate - in the middle of the night - despite the AZ Freedom Caucus offering several amendments to make it better.In the end, the Swamp was successful, but the AZFC fought a hard and very public battle against it every step of the way. What's the moral to this story? Even with a highly organized and disciplined Arizona Freedom Caucus, the Swamp can still win when RINOs and Democrats scheme together. However, that doesn't mean we don't stop fighting. If you can't win, you need to expose the Swamp to the voters. And that's what the AZ Freedom Caucus did and will continue to do. Perhaps most importantly, this budget fight highlights the need for House Freedom Caucus member, Congressman Andy Biggs, to win the governor's race in 2026. A "Governor Biggs + Arizona Freedom Caucus" combination will go a LONG way in cleaning up Arizona and making it great again.
---
---
|
---
**SUPREME COURT DECISIONS** The U.S. Supreme Court issued a slew of decisions this week, several of which impact the states. Here are a couple of notable ones: Our **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** applauded the Court's decision allowing states to defund Planned Parenthood from within Medicaid. SCFC Chairman Jordan Pace [sent a letter](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjlWz5sk7c74Yn1R12O7m5slIgqmRxTIMwZJTT9NxLmiOhNqISJT-2BUO40QQJgVviF8g-3D-3Dd2PH_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHervLIcXXvR6xm4eVUOXkajhx-2FZi7vGxEsWGLhk-2BKK4oySo-2Fro23jwIZlrI7-2Bv5HBw40Gh67ZMnebk13GbemQidvVYbalsL2AL4pQC8J1XpYEUxN2wJmtBdV-2FudVBcXj-2F0jD4BpxNHcV-2BVdJf78TAuXRFgzp5jqwKZdDsEJcrs2B1AIeEUu8pXXn7j2dj18llasASE6XzirF65foj7slO2dnKljltFe-2F4dskmrkcggt8lw-3D) to State Attorney General Alan Wilson demanding that all taxpayer funds sent to Planned Parenthood since 2018 be returned. Our **Georgia Freedom Caucus** [celebrated](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjja-2FX-2BHiJMkQeHavsUeprX-2Bmb6rZOv5CYPNdPI-2Bv5JW8-2BmbmOk2ZW3jGvMWcYgb9GV68ZzSNogF9s4r3Vg9UYro-3DHHv6_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHervLIcXXvR6xm4eVUOXkajhx-2FZi7vGxEsWGLhk-2BKK4oySo-2Fro23jwIZlrI7-2Bv5HBw40Gh67ZMnebk13GbemQidvapuYMMyBji1RfDGVSoY5Wm1OVezJtT8e1z97wttbnUZTbt-2B3uZqOxwhH5uAYjuBeFFKXDmYD-2Fl85FrQ4zUOHG2KZgiWK-2F2WOKNgXtRhy5Q9gH17ih6TBUMFoV3vqFQi9gn3zeOd8qJd5hXANBIadhg-3D) the Court's decision upholding Tennessee's right to ban transgender surgeries for minors. The GAFC reminded Georgia voters that the practice still continues in their state because of one liberal Republican lawmaker who blocked the GAFC's efforts to stop it. The **Maryland Freedom Caucus** reminded voters that they tried to stop HB 161 this session, which would prevent parents from opting their children out of gender and sexuality instruction in public schools. Thankfully the Supreme Court decided this week that parents can indeed opt-out. Read the MD Freedom Caucus's statement [here](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjiwkZmtXDP4u12gaI7rwUjae8XQZaRZzQyAlLxNMAq3Uuj0x4jHFRiKX37EwzEsjeaZTKce3pQPu2qxl1SnrvAA-3D7we1_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHervLIcXXvR6xm4eVUOXkajhx-2FZi7vGxEsWGLhk-2BKK4oySo-2Fro23jwIZlrI7-2Bv5HBw40Gh67ZMnebk13GbemQidve5Uetj7bVlduLHnxYBFHltzTWXfiEoVMhST-2FoVfI3d7yviyKiLir9eEA1WPgoBkdBTqSS3K-2BKD3LIaqt8cNZhyLZKecV-2FnQG50U9yCsnNL0yAdnC8Qx2dbTdNxoNEEX1zCbPnavJC1TmTryD-2FQ8iZ4-3D).

But we can’t do it without you.

Grassroots donors like you keep us going strong. Every dollar counts—especially now.

Can we count on your support today?

accountable. But I can’t do it alone. Democracy doesn’t defend itself —

Hey team,

I’m reaching out about the End of Quarter deadline. [**If you’ve heard enough and want to help us reach our goal, you can make a contribution right now.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/110444181/554359427/1920731667?refcode=IDCCA_EMAIL_280625_FR_EOQ-2&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDU1NzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYzI4YTFmNjMtNGE1NC1mMDExLThmN2MtNjA0NWJkZmU4ZTljIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=yIvNqHUmYlpO4131x1DLk2rvj0eimeSpUHdssX5o1is=)

If you want to hear a little more, here’s a quick rundown of where your contribution goes:
* Towards programs like our Boot Camp which trains new candidates and operatives every year to win campaigns.
* Towards our Vote By Mail program, which targets likely Democratic voters in small and medium sized counties.
* Towards our Rural Grants Program, which funds 10 of our smallest County Parties to help them build sustainable infrastructure to get Democrats elected.

Team: We must pay attention to President Trump's words, taking them literally and figuratively. Why? When we called out a frightening bill, last known as H.R. 9495, **that already passed the House and would give President Donald Trump broad powers to target his political foes,** a lot of our supporters replied that the bill would only truly apply to terrorist groups and that we were overreacting. Well -- earlier this year, right outside the White House, President Trump said people vandalizing Tesla brand cars would be branded domestic terrorists and "go through hell." We're not condoning vandalism, but it shows how quickly and abruptly Donald Trump will escalate against people he sees as his opponents. So we ask again -- **what would stop President Trump from doing the same to nonprofits like ours?** Or other nonprofit groups that oppose his agenda? Tough fights don’t scare me and my service isn’t done. I’m running for the U.S. Senate at a critical moment in our nation’s history. President Trump has taken bold action to protect American lives, secure our borders, and put our country first. Jon Ossoff hasn’t been with him any step of the way. Ossoff stood by while Biden opened our borders and was nowhere to be found when it mattered most during Afghanistan’s collapse. Since the election, all he’s done is vote against supporting Israel and protecting girls’ sports. And by the way, he’s also said he’d support impeaching President Trump. Jon Ossoff is a politician who only cares about optics and keeping the party bosses happy. We can, and we must, do better than that. And I can do better than him. Flipping this Senate seat, defeating Jon Ossoff, and sending President Trump backup is going to make for the most difficult and expensive race in the country. Ossoff will raise and spend whatever it takes. We don’t have to outraise him, but we must raise as much as we can as soon as we can to share my message. And unlike Ossoff, who has elite liberal donors, I depend on patriots like you to fuel the mission. Thank you, Maj. Gen. Regardless of political party, our leaders must have moral standards. Full stop.
Peter,

Earlier this year, Governor Andy Beshear went on _MSNBC_ and called it like it is: **Today’s GOP is more focused on party loyalty than on the people they were elected to serve.**

And since then, _they’ve only proven him right:_
1. **The House GOP voted for a budget that takes food away from hungry families—while exploding the nation’s debt.**
2. **That same bill guts Medicaid, threatening the healthcare coverage of 16 million Americans.**
3. **Just this week, Sen. Mitch McConnell, in a closed-door meeting with other Republicans, said that cuts to healthcare have to stay, and that Americans who lose life-saving healthcare will “get over it.”**

This isn’t just about one bad leader. It’s a pattern that has infected our politics for too long.

Peter,

Republicans are rushing their disastrous budget scam through the Senate,
aiming to pass nearly $1 trillion in devastating cuts to Medicaid, food
assistance, and vital services by July 4th.

The good news? This fight isn’t over. Republicans still face major hurdles
— and we’re mobilizing grassroots opposition nationwide to speak out loud
and clear: Vote NO on these dangerous cuts.

deadline to help power this work?

In red and blue districts nationwide, working people are speaking out
against this bill. Even some Republicans — like Senator Josh Hawley — are
starting to voice concerns, as medical providers in their own communities
raise the alarm.

The pressure is working, but we can’t slow down now.

The GOP knows support is slipping. And while every day that goes by brings
them closer to a vote, it also gives us a chance to put the pressure on
and overwhelm them with opposition.

We’re giving this fight everything we’ve got, but holding the GOP

the movement behind us.

subject: Time is running out
body:
If we can’t show strength now then they will come at us with everything

| | | | [](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/aIWi/?__vbtrk=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
---
Friend, time is quickly running out until we close the book on this fundraising quarter and just how much cash House Republicans were able to bring in these past few months will be public.

**[The media will analyze it, the Democrats will weaponize it, and it will shape the battlefield going forward.](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/aIWi/?__vbtrk=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)**
That’s why this moment matters so much.********We’re currently in the fight of our lives to hold the House and if we don’t look strong at this moment, we’ll signal weakness. That would invite attacks and jeopardize everything we’ve fought for.

Every left-wing Super PAC in the country will be watching to see whether House Republicans look strong - _or vulnerable_.

Our movement has made massive unprecedented progress. But progress isn’t the same as victory...

**[We want TOTAL VICTORY!](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/aIWi/?__vbtrk=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)**
We are locking down the border.
We are dismantling the bloated agencies abusing the American people.
We are crushing the anti-American chaos on college campuses and cities like Los Angeles.
But if we lose the House Democrats will do everything they can to usher in a level of chaos that would rival the very worst days of Joe Biden's presidency.

**[If we can’t show strength now then they will come at us with everything.](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/aIWi/?__vbtrk=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)**
So we’re asking you - urgently and directly:

**_[Please chip in a contribution of whatever you can manage before the deadline to help us finish this quarter strong and protect the House majority](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/aIWi/?__vbtrk=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)_.**

[RUSH YOUR END-OF-QUARTER DONATION](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/aIWi/?__vbtrk=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=Mjk5Mzg2OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)
This isn’t about one race. We need to win the fights in**_New York,_** in**_California_** , in _**Texas**_ , and in**_Pennsylvania_** among others. We must defend seats from the _**suburbs**_ to the _**heartland**_ \- in _**every battleground district**_ where the Left thinks they can buy their way back into power.
They’re counting on**fatigue**.
They’re counting on**apathy**.
They’re counting on voters like you not getting in the fight due to a belief that we’ve already won. Don’t give them that satisfaction.
We are counting on patriots like you remaining in the fight. Right now, we need one more push of support this quarter.
Fellow patriot, you know exactly what is at stake so let's finish strong and DEFEND THE HOUSE!

_In the fight,_
**The House GOP Battleground Fund**

body:
This is big news in our race.

Peter, it’s getting real. **We have another potential Republican opponent.**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250628-2?refcode=em-20250628-2&refcode2=238_1086043_tmUV77&akid=238%2E1086043%2EtmUV77)

His website even says, **“We the people _want a governor with white hair..._ so they have empathy for us.”** Whatever that means.
Marylanders are smart enough to know that the amount of hair someone has isn’t indicative of their ability to lead this state.
Not only is this dog-whistle rhetoric out of touch, _it’s also inaccurate._
Wes has faced and overcome more hardship than most politicians ever will. He lost his father at just three years old. He felt handcuffs on his wrists at 11. He served in combat overseas. And every step of the way, he’s carried those experiences with him.
**Peter, the old guard wants to undo the progress we’ve made with Wes.** They’re not afraid to discount his experience (or even his lack of hair) in an effort to make sure we go back to the broken old politics of yesterday.
**[If you agree Maryland doesn’t need another white-haired governor, please, rush a contribution before our upcoming end-of-quarter deadline. >>](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250628-2?refcode=em-20250628-2&refcode2=238_1086043_tmUV77&akid=238%2E1086043%2EtmUV77)**

**We need _your_ grassroots support to power our reelection effort.**

Peter,

I know the last few weeks have been rough for all of us, and it seems like the news cycle is one tragedy after another right now. For those of us who care deeply about our communities, it’s an incredibly tough time. When I worry about the future of our country, or when things look particularly bleak, I try to find solace in faith and prayer. As I prepare for church tomorrow, I find myself reflecting on a particular passage of scripture from Matthew: | _‘For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in, I needed clothes and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to visit me.’

Then the righteous will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink? When did we see you a stranger and invite you in, or needing clothes and clothe you? When did we see you sick or in prison and go to visit you?’

body:
#
One of the most important things to communicate is that **there is no action that’s too small.**
I think sometimes people talk themselves out of things because they feel like: “What can my one letter do? What can my one call to Congress do? What can my one donation or me showing up to a toy drive, or me showing up to an event _actually_ do?”
It does a lot. Because it inspires other people to show up. **It’s like each drop in the ocean thinking that it’s meaningless, when it’s actually the most powerful force on the planet.**
And that’s the key. If you’re speaking up online, that’s wonderful. How are you integrating this into your life?
That, I think, is where we start to see real change happen.

Alexandria

| | _**Putting Students First and Meeting Energy Demands**_
---
Friends, In a major win for Hoosier students and families, Governor Mike Braun announced on Tuesday that Indiana’s public colleges and universities had agreed to freeze in-state undergraduate tuition and fees for the 2025–2026 and 2026–2027 academic years. This marks the first time since 2010 that so many campuses have done so, delivering on Governor Braun’s commitment to keep college affordable and setting a national precedent. Student leaders praised the move as a step toward greater opportunity for all Hoosiers. The freeze has been backed unanimously by the Indiana Commission for Higher Education, and includes all 15 of the state's public colleges and universities. On Wednesday, Governor Mike Braun announced the creation of the Strategic Energy Growth Task Force to develop a comprehensive plan that meets Indiana’s rapidly growing demand for reliable and affordable energy. With increased electricity needs driven by the return of manufacturing, AI-powered data centers, and consumer electrification, the task force will take an "all-of-the-above" approach to energy development. Its priorities include strengthening energy reliability, maintaining and expanding power generation, deploying nuclear energy, and positioning Indiana as a future energy export state. Thanks to your efforts, our conservative leadership is delivering for Hoosiers, and it's up to us to keep that momentum going into 2026! As always, thank you for being a part of our team. Please feel free to reach out if there's anything I can assist with.
---
| |
---
| | Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman

| | _**Governor Braun Announces Tuition Freeze**_
---
---
Governor Mike Braun announced a two-year tuition freeze for all 15 of Indiana’s public colleges and universities, covering the 2025–26 and 2026–27 academic years. The freeze includes both flagship and regional campuses and follows Braun’s call for schools to cut costs without lowering quality. Tuition at Indiana schools ranges from $2,577 at Ivy Tech to $12,144 at IU Bloomington, all below the national average. Braun emphasized that schools should not raise other fees to make up the difference. “The commitment made by all of Indiana’s public colleges and universities puts students and parents first and demonstrates to the rest of the country that Indiana is a leader in providing a high-quality education at an affordable price." \- Governor Braun via a [recent statement.](http://links.email.in-gop.com/s/c/zJYhPkEeDRUKO9SwHeLlvJjwCdz55pnfUuOoIA7RqmbC02OqEryFZkghbxOXSmxDuqBdXTCtLqJXWUiRedfh9k088gbkPUSNICM0tKhtKIM9t0A0_Rkp1uiFJBLJns7USuWEBor4njtPrFWevh4YXWxCOR7GeJKHOUnR1YFahuWQfn003Fs8Mz-626kkq6JgYl5jlc1qb37eWZf1W6dsiAiLKyFtWt2SzQrvi2XVZQurL4uvL_pFDPbW1_QPlLOp87xt4G9i1_kWnkB68Uc6VAOI1ccoVBZfR2yLzvSQO0o7pdxFXxo_j19LMqH4RUO26I-vaFVYRjjOEOYUoNdFn4Kkq_xYd2uPiTZNbe57I4j3ce-XpwGu5n5NsT8CB9TmZn98I-5W6ivPpauCcbe9PfRPTd_4duDX5ZonfrY_VouCAAORKgdYwLkU-t4a0p8UAI51HUJ5zzNZ_Zw0j6J5f88TqFfCNNt-Gv8CCYQJWzOUJwpKWlHcnsoBmWP4pAKbGdY9YFnEadTNmRSDYbKQF1zdvHDdzSO-ViL0/w7sNAL0luE_f9Njqxxn48uIxZv8XRfvb/10)[](http://links.email.in-gop.com/s/c/RGX0cqqhpCE5J8vcA6ZtRsKPdTAhCQI-5iEPL27VxKw9tsEvkv4uO6cHIb0hLSqkYCI780U3YqfHDFekkewP75ZVrxMx9AwTXRBqc-nlwJh4rBbOQTffXllYGcBg2cKvMRE04VOnsgc6HfZ9q4JB1YcpsjBISj2HIbq1LcfszS1Qu1QVPAJjB72kPF0GejgYzJXJcsgdsitDKtd9da_s259-zStG1qMoJmGtB1cjKj9VzsApPTtWaXiIbleAE_1-oMwHzDGhuU4QWwq7bZvB21XkdTaWD0BOKop5wd_8oA3FQCgTQfgL6oRJMZ77eDHc2JvsG_OhVONkcnShdLJfLvPRe71eRxfWtyX5gTlcUrSP0JC5OoDVljc1W-NEwECLk4v4LFBfJVgzU0bn_JCJ6KTvs4LIBjyGVqSVGI3aQA/fWa8P7xg4094Q4R6iazJfVGoTmsaIGKX/10)

_**Governor Braun Creates Strategic Energy Task Force**_
---
---
Governor Mike Braun has established the Strategic Energy Growth Task Force to ensure reliable and affordable energy as Indiana’s economy expands. The group will develop 5- and 20-year plans focusing on energy reliability, affordability, nuclear development, and making Indiana an energy export state. It will work with utilities and stakeholders to meet rising demand and keep electricity costs down. “Indiana’s economy is growing and we need new solutions to meet this accelerating energy demand reliably and affordably.” \- Governor Mike Braun via [Fox 59.](http://links.email.in-gop.com/s/c/-cEuJhpwTjaeLhC7HfsLLPYkL2yx1ap7ZdGAu4IsagDUpF8Oe_9rYAMYrQ6WE77RSlnvbbJ5mWpeT41zLhqcQYqzzjtvEpqNimT2GbDj0c39vIKL_X0u-4obt1ZuIYXQYkqyq34hBH7h5NwjNXQgUyB9hCJ66Aq85StE_SLJKyle5nIHoGiv3PJeXJs61bQdXgx3PMPd1oWdwhTHxO20jO4c5RbsWEQ--cumUoj98Ahv1VlPE8a1BHVNfTFa8T3abccdaVnV9SkOsx7qqcmKhOy7m79u4zDS4BT_deGIh_Yc3AagA0qZ6pwYzv1C-mA9_qbt-o7FyejjwSe4HjKb5kVS9yrRMUo0ejFGD7epsrgFaB0PtKuaX-JKxtEMKKjUNTiyYKVGrx2PXZ684W_wCKBdsi2N0hu0pc-1cLNJcKOI-4U0RQQiFaec0fHVr8FLen0sKCVwcg8oDe5kl_XRNKNbsVPne8pNKuLCqlz-nNnNaUa3Jbs3GjY-8tPQunmIckLYPIvXc16ymnEvLes0Ytm8sTl-2zx-i9TxC-VeZA/F6A0MPEA7MfgK3vH7l3X0h8oZBb6jWHw/10)

subject: Will you chip in $25?
body:
Please see a special message from our sponsor:

Unsubscribe
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xul=2qq8ny363wdaxf3eu1ztoj205e5mds3ffgevx070sqm45o3xzr89jt0814qcborgyd4vhxrwzu6z51uae5o708o3mipf89356p65lmljo&__stmp=syl3rc&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh
